The gain fails because the input-to-feedback resistor ratio is about 20× too large. For an inverting amplifier, the simulated gain of -0.02657 matches -Rf/R1 = -1059.2/37903 ≈ -0.0279 (the small difference is finite open-loop gain). The target range of -0.00104 to -0.00156 requires R1 between about 679 kΩ and 1.02 MΩ for the given Rf. The midpoint is about 814 kΩ.

The other specs are consistent with a healthy amplifier core: bandwidth, power, and offset all pass, so the op-amp itself is likely intact. Rx doesn't affect gain because vin2 is unused, and Rz/Cc shape bandwidth and compensation rather than the closed-loop gain. I ranked them after R1 on that basis.

```json
{"ranking": ["R1", "Rf", "Rx"], "fault": "R1 is wrong in value: 37903 Ohm was used, which makes the closed-loop gain -Rf/R1 ≈ -0.028 instead of the required -0.00104 to -0.00156 V/V. For Rf = 1059.2 Ohm, R1 should be about 8.1e5 Ohm (valid range roughly 6.8e5 to 1.02e6 Ohm)."}
```
